newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-U.K. rates seen higher on consumer demand.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-U.K. rates seen higher on consumer demand.

text.p: British interest rates are expected to climb further this year as inflation fed by consumer demand rises above official targets, a Reuters survey showed.
By third quarter 1997 base rates are expected to rise to seven percent compared with six percent now, the median of 35 forecasts contributed by economists to the survey showed.
Interest rates will then stabilise at these levels for 12 months until third quarter 1998.

"We already have inflationary pressures in the economy, and what is more we have a potentially huge surge in consumer spending coming up, which will fuel price pressures," said Richard Jeffrey, group economist at Charterhouse.

Rising house prices, cash windfalls from building society flotations and personal income growth will all help to boost consumer demand, analysts said in their forecasts, which were gathered between January 6 and 8.
In late December the Halifax Building Society forecast house prices would rise between six and eight percent in 1997 on top of the seven percent rises already seen in 1996.
Core inflation -- retail prices excluding mortgage interest payments -- is forecast at three percent in the third and fourth quarters of 1997, the survey showed.
By comparison, official government forecasts see core inflation at 2.5 percent in the last quarter of this year.
A few analysts expect the government to hold interest rates at six percent until after the general election, due by May.

But a large majority, 27 out of 35, expect base rates at 6.25 percent or higher by March and 28 out of 34 expect base rates at 6.50 percent or higher by mid-1997, when the election victor will have taken office.

"The new government, whatever colour, will have to take pretty aggressive action to try to control consumer spending and the only immediate action they can take is to raise interest rates," said Charterhouse's Jeffrey.
Some economists believe seven percent interest rates will be enough to bring inflation back to, or under, the official target.
But Stuart Wetherby, UK economist at Panmure Gordon, expects base rates to rise to 8.30 percent in the second half of 1998.
"If they want to meet their inflation target there will have to be some pretty dramatic rises in interest rates," he said.
Wetherby predicts a peak in core inflation at 3.5 percent in third quarter 1997.
By end-1998, the survey shows base rates at 6.75 percent.

Three-month LIBOR -- London interbank offered rate -- is forecast to peak at 7.27 percent by the end of this year, the mean of forecasts showed. By end-1997 three-month LIBOR will fall back under seven percent to 6.91 percent.
